chunks: Acknowledgements India stands at a defining demographic juncture. With a median age of 28.4 years in 2024 and a population of over 1.45 billion, the nation is home to one of the world’s youngest populations—more than 40% are below 25 years of age, and over 50% are under 35. This demographic dividend holds the promise of unparalleled growth and innovation. However, it also underscores a significant challenge: the growing gap between education and employability. Despite abundant opportunities across both formal and informal sectors, India continues to face one of the world’s largest shortages of skilled manpower. As highlighted in the India Skills Report 2025, only 54.81% of young Indians are considered employable, revealing an urgent need to align learning outcomes with workplace realities. The imperative of our times is to reimagine education as a pathway to employability, enterprise, and empowerment. Skill-oriented learning must become both accessible and aspirational—from the school level through to higher education. In this context, the proactive initiatives of the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) deserve special recognition. By introducing 44 skill courses at the

n this context, the proactive initiatives of the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) deserve special recognition. By introducing 44 skill courses at the Senior Secondary level, CBSE has taken a visionary step towards integrating practical competencies with academic learning. This initiative not only equips students with real-world capabilities but also broadens their awareness of emerging career possibilities. The ultimate objective of skill education is to cultivate confident, capable, and responsible young citizens—individuals who can adapt, innovate, and contribute meaningfully to a rapidly transforming world. Such an education system will not merely prepare students for livelihoods; it will prepare them for life itself. PREFACE The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) now offers 44 skill subjects in classes XI and XII with the objective of helping students build problem-solving and critical-thinking skills and making them aware of the career possibilities around the world. In fact, skill education at CBSE envisions imparting the procedural knowledge and skills to the students that will enable them to excel and emerge successful in real situations at both work and life. The focus is on imparting an education that is holistic, meaningful, and skill-oriented, which instills among the students a sense of usefulness and responsibility. This Compendium of Career & Education Pathways for Skill Subjects has been made with the objective of not only providing students with the skill courses available as part of the CBSE curriculum for classes XI and XII; but also information about the courses in such a manner that it piques the interest of the students for taking up such courses. Keeping that aim in mind, the compendium also provides additional information about career and education pathways that are possible in the field, domain or the industry to which the skill subject belongs. So, for each skill

al information about career and education pathways that are possible in the field, domain or the industry to which the skill subject belongs. So, for each skill subject, there is an introduction to the field, domain or the industry to which the skill subject belongs, to begin with. This is followed by the outline of the career pathway, along with the job description of the job role under consideration. And finally, the education pathway applicable for the entire career pathway is outlined in terms of the courses that can be done along with an indicative list of colleges and universities where one can do these courses. This is followed by insights into the technical and soft skills needed. Thereafter, information is shared on some other careers that are possible in other domains, with the same education and experience as the present one. And finally, the future prospects with the skill subject are explained. (ii)

Message from Chairperson Education today extends far beyond academic achievement. It must equip learners with practical skills, critical thinking abilities, creativity, and the confidence to navigate real-world challenges. Skill-based education plays a pivotal role in this transformation by enabling students to apply knowledge meaningfully and develop capabilities that are essential for both employment and life. By engaging with skill-based subjects, students gain hands-on experience in areas such as communication, problem-solving, technical competencies, and vocational practices. This not only enhances their readiness for the workplace but also opens up multiple pathways for career progression immediately after school. Importantly, it nurtures a spirit of self-reliance and encourages entrepreneurial thinking—qualities that are vital in today's dynamic and evolving world. In this context, I am pleased to note CBSE's initiative in developing the “Compendium of Career and Education Pathways After Skill Subjects in Class XII.” This resource comes at a crucial juncture when students are making important decisions about their future. It provides clear visibility into a wide spectrum of

This resource comes at a crucial juncture when students are making important decisions about their future. It provides clear visibility into a wide spectrum of opportunities across domains such as technology, healthcare, business, agriculture, and the creative industries. The compendium is designed to empower students with informed choices and broaden their horizons beyond conventional career routes. It will also help parents and educators better understand and support diverse aspirations, thereby creating an ecosystem that values multiple pathways to success. I encourage students, teachers, and parents to actively engage with this compendium - use it not just as a guide, but as a catalyst to explore possibilities, make thoughtful decisions, and build fulfilling careers grounded in skills and purpose. With best wishes, Shri Rahul Singh, I.A.S. Chairman, CBSE (iii)

As the landscape of education and employment continues to evolve, the need to align learning with real-world application has become more critical than ever. Skill education is not merely an addition to the academic framework—it is an essential pathway that enables students to translate knowledge into capability and aspiration into opportunity. At CBSE, our focus has been on systematically strengthening this pathway. The introduction of 43 skill subjects at the senior secondary level reflects a conscious effort to provide students with meaningful exposure to diverse domains and emerging industries. These subjects are designed not only to build technical proficiency but also to develop adaptability, problem-solving ability, and a deeper understanding of how different sectors function in practice. The “Compendium of Career and Education Pathways After Skill Subjects in Class XII” is a continuation of this effort. It has been developed as a practical and structured resource to support students at a critical point of transition—from school to higher education and careers. The compendium seeks to bring clarity to the often complex and fragmented information surrounding career options

on—from school to higher education and careers. The compendium seeks to bring clarity to the often complex and fragmented information surrounding career options linked to skill-based education. What makes this resource particularly valuable is its focus on connecting three critical dimensions—subjects, careers, and educational pathways. By mapping these linkages clearly, it enables students to see not just immediate options, but also long-term trajectories. It also provides insights into the competencies required, the nature of roles across industries, and the evolving opportunities that students can aspire to. Equally important is the role this compendium can play for educators and parents. By offering a comprehensive view of opportunities, it helps build confidence in skill-based pathways and encourages more informed guidance and support for students. This initiative is a step towards making career decision-making more informed, inclusive, and aligned with individual strengths and interests. I encourage all stakeholders to engage deeply with this compendium and use it as a tool to expand perspectives, discover possibilities, and make thoughtful choices. . With best wishes, Dr.

A. Purpose of the Compendium Introduction Keeping in view the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, the Government of India has introduced the National Curriculum Framework for School Education (NCF–SE), a comprehensive framework to guide India's school education system in 2023. In line with this framework, the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has introduced skill education to align with the goals of NEP 2020 and NCF-SE, and prepare students for future challenges and opportunities by bridging the gap between academic knowledge and real-world application. So, CBSE now offers 44 skill subjects in classes XI and XII with the objective of helping students build problem-solving and critical-thinking skills and making them aware of the career possibilities in today’s world. In fact, skill education at CBSE envisions imparting the procedural knowledge and skills to enable the students to excel and emerge successful in real situations at work and life. Skill-based learning is crucial for an individual’s progress, equipping individuals with practical, applicable skills that enhance employability, adaptability, and innovation, ultimately leading to a more skilled and competitive

ing individuals with practical, applicable skills that enhance employability, adaptability, and innovation, ultimately leading to a more skilled and competitive workforce. In today's rapidly evolving and dynamic job market, employers increasingly prioritise practical skills and experience over theoretical knowledge alone. Skill-based learning directly addresses this need by equipping individuals with the skills demanded by industries. Further, developing in-demand skills opens doors to better job opportunities, higher salaries, and career advancement. B. Importance of Skill-Based Learning and Career Awareness The purpose of this Compendium of Career & Education Pathways for Skill Subjects is therefore to provide students with information on the skill courses available as part of the CBSE curriculum for XII in such a manner that it piques the interest of the students for taking up one such course and creates aspiration within them to take up a career that the particular course leads to. Keeping that aim in mind, the compendium also provides additional information about career and education pathways that are possible in the field and domain or the industry to which the skill subject

um also provides additional information about career and education pathways that are possible in the field and domain or the industry to which the skill subject belongs. The other thing that is notable today is the pace of change in technology and processes involved in doing work. Skill-based learning fosters adaptability, enabling individuals to quickly learn new skills and adapt to changing job requirements. Acquiring new skills also boosts confidence, broadens horizons, and leads to a greater sense of personal fulfilment. And finally, skill-based learning extends beyond vocational training, encompassing essential life skills like communication, problem-solving, and critical thinking. Along with skill-based learning, today’s students also need career awareness. With many careers already there than before and new ones emerging with the frenetic pace at which the world is changing, career awareness is crucial for informed decision-making, helping individuals understand their strengths, interests, and potential career paths, leading to a more fulfilling and successful future. (v)

C. Alignment with NEP 2020 and CBSE Skill Subjects CBSE skill subjects are aligned with NEP 2020's focus on integrating voc ational skills into the school curriculum, aiming to bridge the gap between academic knowledge and real-world applications, thereby preparing students for future challenges and India's vision of becoming a global leader in skill development. To achieve this alignment, CBSE is coming up with the following initiatives: D. Integration Of Academic and Vocational Domain The integration of academic and vocational domains refers to frameworks like India's National Credit Framework (NCrF) that all ow students to combine credits earned from general education, vocational training, and work experience for academic or professional progression. This approach aims to create flexible pathways between learning and work, improving student employability by providing practical skills alongside theoretical knowledge and recognising diverse learning experiences. Key mechanisms include offering vocational courses in secondary schools, using credit-based systems for accumulation and transfer, and fostering partnerships between educational institutions and industry. The CBSE Skill

dary schools, using credit-based systems for accumulation and transfer, and fostering partnerships between educational institutions and industry. The CBSE Skill Subjects are a step in this direction. NEP Mandatory Skill Labs: CBSE mandates schools to set up "Composite Skill Labs" for classes 6-12, aligning with NEP 2020 and NCF-SE guidelines, emphasizing practical skills alongside traditional subjects. Skill Subjects as Mandatory: The guidelines advocate for the inclusion of skill subjects as a mandatory part of the curriculum from class VI onwards. Bridging the Gap: The integration of skill subjects aims to bridge the gap between theory and practice, equipping students with practical skills and real-world experience. Web Portal: CBSE is providing a web portal for registration and certification of students who have opted for Skill Modules. Skill Hubs and National Credit Framework: CBSE is actively facilitating Skill Hubs initiatives in schools and is looking forward to operationalising the National Credit Framework (NCrF) to enable the integration of academic and vocational domains. (NCrF) to enable the integration of academic and vocational domains. Joint Certification: Students completing Class X or XII with Skill subjects are awarded an additional certificate jointly signed by CBSE and the relevant Industry/Organisation. Introducing Contemporary Subjects: CBSE offers a variety of skill subjects, including those related to Retail, Information Technology, Marketing & Sales, Banking, Finance, and AI. Focus on 21st Century Skills: NEP 2020 emphasizes the importance of developing 21st-century skills like critical thinking, problem-solving, creativity, and innovation, which are also promoted through CBSE's skill education initiatives. (vi)

E. How to use this compendium effectively? This compendium has been organised into 6 domain/industry clusters, within which are the details of careers mapped to each skill subject. For each career, there is an explan ation of what the career involves, to begin with. This is followed by the description of relevant skill-based subjects in the CBSE curriculum and then the education pathway. Next, it goes into the details of the technical and soft skills required. This is followed by creating an awareness of job roles and industry sectors where the jobs are available, and the future trends and growth prospects in those sectors. Next, it takes a look at some of the well-known institutions offering the courses that help a student make the chosen career and possible internship opportunities by way of government schemes, corporate programs and apprenticeships. And finally there are some success stories of professionals in the field. The compendium can thus be used to know about any aspect of a career of interest. (vii)

Introduction Vice President - Retail Sales Retail is the sale of goods and services by a business to people who want them. A retailer is a person, shop, store, company or an ecommerce site that buys products from a manufacturer or wholesaler and sells them to end users or customers in relatively small quantities for use or consumption rather than for resale and makes a profit in the process. 1 There are different types of retailers depending upon the sales model they use and the different consumer types they cater to. They each provide different experiences—sometimes offering direct purchasing from a manufacturer, or providing a wide range of merchandise. They include: (1) Grocery Stores: These retaile rs sell all types of food and beverage products (2) Supermarkets: The supermarket s sell home products and consumer electronics as well (3) Department Stores: Traditional department store s sell a wide range of merchandise that is arranged by category into different sections in the physical retail space. For example, some categories in a ladies’ department store are clothing, beauty products, jewelry, handbags, shoes and more. (4) Warehouse Retailers: Warehouse-type facilities such

tegories in a ladies’ department store are clothing, beauty products, jewelry, handbags, shoes and more. (4) Warehouse Retailers: Warehouse-type facilities such as Hypermart, stock a large variety of products packaged in large quantities and sold at prices lower than retail. They generally sell in bulk or in quantities not otherwise available in other retail outlets.

2 (5) Specialty/Outlet Retailers: These specialize in a specific category and brand-name products. Lenskart and Bata are examples of specialty retailers, generally selling only merchandise that carries their brand name (6) Discount Retailer: Discounters sell a wide variety of products that are often privately labeled or generic brands at below- retail prices (7) Internet/Mobile Retailer: Internet shopping website s ship the purchases directly to customers at their homes or workplaces, without the expenses of traditional brick-and-mortar retailers. They usually sell merchandise for a lower-than-retail price, using warehouses for storage and developing relationships with warehouses, vendors, and sometimes manufacturers to provide goods at reduced prices. (8) Luxury Retail: Luxury retail is about building up an “exclusive” image for the brand being marketed by putting forth different facets of the product whether that’s heritage, craftmanship, quality, aesthetics, rarity, extraordinariness or the way it makes the customer feel. Rising retail sales generally suggest a healthy economy with strong consumer confidence, while declining sales can indicate economic slowdown. Retail sales directly measure consumer spending, a significant component of GDP and a major driver of economic growth. Changes in it provide insights into the overall health of the economy, including trends in employment, income, and inflation. So, investors analyze retail sales data to assess market sentiment and make informed investment decisions. And policymakers use retail sales data to inform monetary and fiscal policy decisions, such as adjusting interest rates or government spending.

3 Vice President - Retail: What’s the Career About? The entry-level position in the retail sales function is that of a Retail Sales Associate. A Retail Sales Associate is a front-line employee who helps customers in a store or retail setting by providing product information, customer service, and support during the purchase process. Their main goal is to ensure a positive shopping experience and help drive sales for the store. In other words, retail sales associates are the face of a store as they greet customers, answer questions about products, and help them find what they need. Though the retail sales associate is the entry-level position of retail business, as every retail business is completely dependent upon the sales they get, this is one of the important positions in this profession After spending a couple of years as a retail sales associate, they advance to the role of a Team Leader. A retail sales Team Leader leads and motivates a team of sales staff to achieve sales targets and ensure excellent customer service. Key responsibilities include managing daily store operations, training and coaching team members, overseeing inventory and merchandising, resolving customer

ce. Key responsibilities include managing daily store operations, training and coaching team members, overseeing inventory and merchandising, resolving customer issues, and reporting performance to management. They are the point person on the floor, responsible for maintaining store standards, motivating staff, and ensuring a positive customer experience. Next, once they have put in 2 to 5 years of experience as a Team Leader, they transition into management positions, overseeing staff, store operations, and sales performance as a Store Supervisor or Floor Manager. A Store Supervisor in retail sales manages a team and the daily operations of a store or department, focusing on sales performance, customer service, inventory control, and staff management to achieve business goals. Their duties include scheduling staff, training new hires, maintaining store appearance, resolving customer issues, and ensuring company policies are followed to create a positive shopping experience and drive sales. A Retail Floor Manager supervises daily store operations to achieve sales targets and profitability by managing staff, ensuring excellent customer service, maintaining inventory and store

rvises daily store operations to achieve sales targets and profitability by managing staff, ensuring excellent customer service, maintaining inventory and store presentation, and implementing policies and procedures. They guide and train employees, resolve customer issues, drive sales initiatives, and ensure overall operational efficiency and compliance. Alternatively, depending on the enterprise and industry, they may also specialise in areas like visual merchandising, inventory management, or customer relationship management. After 3 odd years as a Store Supervisor / Floor Manager, they became an Assistant Store Manager. An Assistant Store Manager in retail sales oversees and manages daily store operations, supporting the Store Manager to achieve sales goals by supervising staff, ensuring excellent customer service, managing inventory, and maintaining the store's physical appearance and organisation. Key responsibilities include training and motivating employees, handling customer complaints, coordinating sales and merchandising efforts, and ensuring compliance with company policies to boost overall store performance and profitability.

4 Their next position is Store Manager. A Retail Store Manager runs a store's daily operations, focusing on profitability and customer satisfaction by managing staff, inventory, sales, and store presentation. Key responsibilities include setting sales goals, analysing sales data, controlling inventory, training staff, handling customer issues, and ensuring compliance with safety regulations and company policies. Essentially, they are the backbone of the store, responsible for everything from motivating sales teams to maintaining a clean and organised environment. After a total experience of about 10 years, the Retail Sales Associates grow into Area Sales Managers. An Area Sales Manager in retail is a leadership role responsible for driving sales revenue and ensuring operational efficiency across multiple stores within a specific geographic area. Their key duties include setting sales targets, leading and coaching sales teams, building strong customer relationships, monitoring performance, implementing sales strategies, and reporting on results to upper management to achieve regional sales goals. After about 15 years of total experience, the retail sales associates become Regional

reporting on results to upper management to achieve regional sales goals. After about 15 years of total experience, the retail sales associates become Regional Manager Retail Sales. A Regional Head of Retail Sales leads and develops strategic sales plans to achieve financial targets, oversees and mentors a regional sales team, manages distribution channels, and strengthens relationships with dealers, retailers, and influencers. They are responsible for driving business growth by analysing market trends, implementing sales strategies, and ensuring high levels of customer and dealer satisfaction within their designated geographic region Their next promotion is as a Zonal Manager, which is a high-level responsibility for retail operations across a large geographic area. A Zonal Manager (ZM) is responsible for driving sales within a specific geographic zone by developing and implementing sales strategies, managing a regional sales team, setting and achieving sales targets, building relationships with retailers and customers, and analysing market trends to expand market share and grow revenue. Key duties include creating sales plans, motivating the sales team, monitoring competitor

, and analysing market trends to expand market share and grow revenue. Key duties include creating sales plans, motivating the sales team, monitoring competitor activity, managing budgets, and collaborating with other departments to align sales efforts with broader business goals. Next, they go on to become a National Sales Manager. A National Sales Manager in retail is a strategic leader who develops and implements nationwide sales strategies to drive revenue growth across all company branches and sales teams. Key responsibilities include setting national sales targets, analysing market trends, managing regional sales managers, fostering strong client and partner relationships, and ensuring nationwide consistency in sales processes and customer service to maximise company profits. After the National Sales Manager comes the Vice President of Sales, who is the overall head of the sales organisation. A VP of Sales in retail oversees sales strategy, leads sales teams, and manages overall revenue for a retail business, focusing on sales growth, customer experience, and profitability. Introduction Equity Dealer/ Mutual Fund Agent - Financial Markets Management Financial markets are a type of marketplace that provide an avenue for the sale and purchase of assets such as shares, bonds, foreign exchange, and derivatives. These markets facilitate the flow of capital and help allocate resources efficiently, supporting economic growth. Essentially, they provide a space for buyers and sellers to connect and trade financial instruments. 29 The prices of these assets are determined by the interactions of supply and demand, with buyers offering bids and sellers offering ask. However, for those investors who do not wish to directly participate in the trading of stocks, bonds, currencies or derivatives, there are mutual funds. Equity Dealers/Mutual Fund Agents: What Are These Careers About? Mutual funds are investment vehicles that pool money from many investors to invest in a diversified portfolio of assets like stocks, bonds, or other securities. These funds are managed by professional fund managers who make investment decisions to generate returns for the investors. Investors buy units in the fund, and each unit represents a proportional share in the fund's total

e investment decisions to generate returns for the investors. Investors buy units in the fund, and each unit represents a proportional share in the fund's total holdings. The total amount of holdings by the mutual fund is called its portfolio. These markets facilitate the trading of various financial instruments, including: Among the key operators in the financial markets are Equity Dealers and Mutual Funds Agents. Equity dealers are financial professionals or firms that buy and sell stocks (equities)—either on behalf of clients or for their own accounts. They execute trades for their clients, either buying stocks to add to a portfolio or selling stocks to liquidate or adjust positions. They stay informed about market conditions, news events, and economic indicators that could impact the value of stocks and other equity instruments. They analyse market trends and use quantitative models to make informed trading decisions. In simple terms, agriculture is the art and science of turning land into a source of sustenance and livelihood. 46 Agriculture is the primary source of livelihood for about 43.5% of India’s population. At the time of our independence this figure was 75%. However, pioneering work by agriculture scientists and the efforts of farmers, in what is popularly known as the “Green Revolution’, helped achieve a breakthrough in the agriculture sector in the 1960s. The nation that was frequently plagued by famines and chronic food shortage before green revolution today produces surplus. India is among the top three global producers of many crops, including wheat, rice, pulses, cotton, peanuts, fruits and vegetables. Worldwide, India had the largest herds of buffalo and cattle, is the largest producer of milk and has one of the largest and fastest growing poultry industries. f milk and has one of the largest and fastest growing poultry industries. The economic contribution of agriculture to India's GDP is steadily declining with the country's broad-based economic growth. The Director of Agricultural Extension: What is the Career About? Agricultural extension is the application of scientific research and new knowledge to agricultural practices through farmer education and communication. It is a process that helps farmers adopt new technologies and farming practices

knowledge to agricultural practices through farmer education and communication. It is a process that helps farmers adopt new technologies and farming practices to improve their production efficiency, income, and overall well-being. It involves sharing information, knowledge, skills, and farm management practices with farmers to enable them to increase their income sustainably. Essentially, it acts as a bridge between scientific research and practical application on the farm. Agricultural extension plays a crucial role in boosting agricultural productivity, increasing food security, improving rural livelihoods, and promoting agriculture as an engine of pro-poor economic growth. The role of agricultural extension workers while living among rural people is to bring necessary change in individual and collective farmer behavior and motivating them. They operate as facilitators and communicators, helping farmers in their decision- making and ensuring that appropriate knowledge is implemented to obtain the best results with regard to sustainable production and general rural development. egard to sustainable production and general rural development. The career of a Director of Agricultural Extension typically follows a path that involves gaining experience, improving skills, and assuming roles with increasing responsibility. The Agricultural Extension Worker is the first-level position in the hierarchy. At this stage, an extension worker is usually responsible for fieldwork, such as visiting farmers' fields, providing advice on crop management, pest control, irrigation, and soil health. They may also conduct surveys, gather data, and assist in training sessions.

From Extension Program Manager/Coordinator, the next position is that of Director of Agricultural Extension within government bodies, international organisations, or large NGOs. A Director of Agricultural Extension leads efforts to transfer farming technology and knowledge to farmers, overseeing extension services, training programs, and information dissemination through various channels like Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) and media to improve agricultural practices and profitability. They also support government agricultural policies and programs, manage extension staff, and ensure the effective application of new technologies in the field. 47 Director of Agricultural Extension: What does the Job Role Involve? The next position that an Agricultural Extension Worker grows into is that of an Extension Officer. At this level, extension officers usually manage a specific geographical area or farming sector (such as horticulture, dairy, or crops). They oversee a team of extension workers, assist in planning and organizing training programs, and ensure that the latest agricultural practices are being disseminated to farmers. The Extension Officers then become an Extension Program

These professionals are responsible for managing extension programs at a regional or national level. Influencer Marketing Influencer Marketing is a form of marketing which places focus on influential people rather than the target market as a whole. The nature of influencer marketing is such that consumers tend to trust influencers more than traditional marketing and advertisements. That’s what makes it powerful, and if done right, it can lead to tremendous business success and growth.

71 A Marketing Executive is an entry-level role where the individual focuses on executing marketing campaigns, conducting market research, and supporting marketing activities and develops skills in digital marketing, content creation, and analytics. In today’s world, the responsibilities of a marketing executive are demanding and involve a lot of juggling between tasks, from writing articles to mastering SEO research and always being ‘on’ in terms of social media. After 2–3 years of experience, marketing executives grow into Senior Marketing Executives, where they take on more responsibility in campaign planning and execution. In addition, they manage small projects and begin mentoring junior team members. They also gain deeper knowledge of brand management and marketing strategies. Then, after 4–6 years of experience, they become Marketing Managers, where they oversee a team of marketing executives and coordinate multiple campaigns. They also develop marketing strategies, manage budgets, and analyse market trends while collaborating with sales, product development, and senior leadership. Next, they become Senior Marketing Managers or Brand Managers after 6–8 years of experience.

After being Senior Marketing Managers or Brand Managers with a total experience of 8 to 12 years, they become Marketing Directors who set the overall marketing strategy for the company or a large division. Introduction GIS Scientist - Geospatial Technology A geographic information system (GIS) is a computer system for capturing, storing, checking, and displaying data related to positions on Earth’s surface. GIS connects data to a map, integrating location data (where things are) with all types of descriptive information (what things are like there). GIS can use any information that includes location. The location can be expressed in many different ways, such as latitude and longitude, address, or PIN code. In fact, many different types of information can be compared and contrasted using GIS. The system can include data about people, such as population, income, or education level. It can include information about the landscape, such as the location of streams, different kinds of vegetation, and different kinds of soil. It can also include information about the sites of factories, farms, and schools, or storm drains, roads, and electric power lines. The key features and functions of a GIS are as follows: 1.Data Capture and Storage: GIS systems can ingest various data formats, including maps, satellite imagery, and tabular data, and store it in a structured manner. 2.Spatial Analysis:

rage: GIS systems can ingest various data formats, including maps, satellite imagery, and tabular data, and store it in a structured manner. 2.Spatial Analysis: GIS tools enable users to perform complex spatial analyses, such as buffer zones, overlaying layers, and identifying spatial patterns. 3.Visualization and Mapping: GIS software allows users to create maps and visualizations that display data in a geographic context, helping to identify trends and patterns. 4.Query and Analysis: GIS systems enable users to query and analyze data based on location and other attributes, providing insights into geographic relationships. 5.Data Integration: GIS can integrate various data sources, allowing users to combine different datasets to create a more comprehensive understanding of geographic phenomena. 100 The benefits of using GIS are: 1.Improved Decision Making: GIS helps organizations make informed decisions by providing a visual representation of data and allowing for spatial analysis. 2.Enhanced Communication: GIS maps and visualizations facilitate clear communication of geographic information, making it easier to understand complex datasets. 3.Cost Savings: By identifying spatial

A GIS Scientist: What is this Career About? A GIS career involves using Geographic Information System (GIS) technology to analyse, interpret, and visualise spatial data to solve problems and make decisions in various fields. As GIS can show many different kinds of data on one map, it enables people to more easily see, analyse, and understand patterns and relationships and geographic context. This can lead to roles in industries like environmental management, urban planning, real estate, and public safety, where GIS helps with tasks such astracking wildlife, planning delivery routes, and optimising resource allocation.

Introduction Project Manager - Electronic Technology - Installations Electronic technology refers to the design, development, and application of electronic devices and systems that use the controlled flow of electrons to perform tasks like processing, storing, and transmitting information or energy. It encompasses a wide range of fields, from simple radios and televisions to complex computers, automation systems and communication networks. The basic components of electronic technology are resistors, capacitors, diodes, transistors, and integrated circuits. It is used in a vast array of applications, including: Telecommunications: Radios, televisions, cell phones, internet. Computers and Information Processing: Hardware, software, data storage. Industry: Automation, robotics, manufacturing. Healthcare: Medical devices, imaging systems, monitoring equipment. Consumer Electronics: Entertainment devices, appliances, wearables. nic Technology – Installations involves the practical, hands-on application of electronic principles to the design, assembly, setup, testing, and maintenance of electronic systems and equipment. This field focuses on the implementation and operation of systems rather than the high-level theory and design done by engineers, encompassing tasks like installing wiring, configuring devices, troubleshooting faults, performing diagnostic tests, and ensuring systems meet performance specifications. A Project Manager for Electronic Technology – Installations plans, executes, and oversees projects involving the setup of electronic systems and hardware, ensuring they are completed on time, within budget, and meet all technical and business goals. Multi-Media - Animator Multimedia refers to the presentation of information by combining text, graphics, images, audio, video and animations by using computers, mobiles, tablets and other audio-visual devices and equipment. It also includes interactive elements such as voice command, mouse manipulation, text entry, touch screen, video capture, or live participation of the user. Some of the sectors where multimedia is used extensively are education, training, reference materials, business presentations, advertising and entertainment. One of the advantages of multimedia is that it can be made interactive. 119 Animation which is one of the important constituents of multimedia nowadays refers to the illusion of movement created by showing a series of still pictures in rapid succession. In traditional animation, pictures are drawn or painted on transparent celluloid sheets to be photographed. Early cartoons are examples of this, but today, most animated movies are made with computer-generated imagery (CGI) Introduction Animators are professional artists who draw and design for different media, such as film, television, video games, social media and marketing content, like commercials.

Animators also work closely with directors, artists and writers to help create personality traits, choose colours and develop plots for the animation. Animators can be specialists in 2-Dimensional, 3-Dimensional or Special Effects. Animators: What’s the Career About? Introduction Director of Taxation A tax is a mandatory fee or financial charge levied by a government on an individual or an organization to collect revenue to generate income for undertaking projects to boost the economy of the country and to raise the standard of living of its citizens. The authority of the government to levy taxes in India is derived from the Constitution of India, which allocates the power to levy taxes to the Central and State governments. All taxes levied within India need to be backed by an accompanying law passed by the Parliament or the State Legislature. Common example of taxes that are levied are wealth taxes, inheritance taxes, estate taxes, gift taxes, property taxes, sales taxes, use taxes, payroll taxes, custom and excise duties etc. 125 Director of Taxation: What Is This Careers About? GST, or Goods and Services Tax, is a specific type of indirect tax imposed on the supply of goods and services in India. It is a tax you pay to the government when you buy things like clothes, food, electronics, or use services like mobile recharge or hotel stays. Introduction Cost Accountant - Cost Accounting Cost accounting is a facet of management accounting that determines the actual cost associated with manufacturing a product or providing a service by assessing the variable costs of each step of production as well as fixed costs. It is done for the purpose of budget preparation and profitability analysis. The information derived from this process is useful to managers in determining which products, departments or services are most profitable and which ones need improvement. So, unlike financial accounting, which provides information to external financial statement users, cost accounting is not required to adhere to set standards and can be flexible to meet the needs of management. 131 Cost Accountant - Cost Accounting: What Is This Career About? Cost accounting is primarily used as a decision-making tool for individuals in charge of business operations. Managers use standardized methods to control cost in order to meet the desired level of profitability. Cost Accountants therefore are also known as Management Accountants. They collect and analyse all financial information for use by the management of the organization they work for.

refore are also known as Management Accountants. They collect and analyse all financial information for use by the management of the organization they work for. While most cost accountants work in government organizations or large companies, some will work as consultants either through public accounting firms or their own independent practice. Private consultants will often be called upon to perform services for small or mid-sized businesses that cannot substantiate the full-time employment of a cost accountant. Cost accountants analyze and manage a company's expenses to improve profitability and financial efficiency. They track costs related to production, labor, and inventory, providing insights for budgeting, pricing, and financial planning. Their work includes analyzing data, identifying cost inefficiencies, and suggesting strategies for cost control. Junior Accountants - Cost Accounting play an important role in helping a company understand, manage, and reduce its costs. While this is typically an entry-level position, it provides a strong foundation in financial analysis and business operations. Junior Accountants - Cost Accounting focus on tracking, analysing, and reporting

it provides a strong foundation in financial analysis and business operations. Junior Accountants - Cost Accounting focus on tracking, analysing, and reporting on a company's costs, especially in manufacturing or service-oriented businesses. They assist in cost allocation, budgeting, variance analysis, and other cost control measures to improve profitability and efficiency. This role is crucial for understanding where costs are being incurred and how to optimise spending. After the Cost Accounting - Junior Accountants have gained about 2 to 4 years of experience they become Cost Accountants/Cost Analysts who focus analysing cost data, monitoring variances, and working on budgeting and pricing decisions. They are expected to have completed CMA or CA-Inter to grow into this position.

Introduction Shorthand (English) - Stenographer Stenography is the practice of writing in shorthand, a method of rapid writing using symbols, abbreviations, or special characters to represent words or phrases. It allows people to transcribe spoken words quickly and accurately, often in real time. A stenographer is a professional who creates a verbatim record of spoken language, typically using a specialised machine called a stenotype or shorthand writing techniques. They are often referred to as court reporters, and their primary role is to document legal proceedings, depositions, and other events where an accurate, real-time record is crucial. A stenographer is a person who makes a written verbatim record using a unique shortened writing style called “steno” on a steno machine. Steno is “written” on the machine using a special theory that is based on syllables, rather than letter by letter, as is done on a typical keyboard. Many forms of shorthand exist. A typical shorthand system provides symbols or abbreviations for words and common phrases, which can allow someone well-trained in the system to write as quickly as people speak. Introduction Service Director - Air-conditioning & Refrigeration Air conditioning and refrigeration are both technologies used for cooling and controlling humidity, but they differ in their primary purpose and application. Air conditioning focuses on cooling and dehumidifying air in enclosed spaces to achieve a more comfortable indoor environment. It is commonly used in homes, offices, vehicles and commercial buildings. Refrigeration focuses on cooling and preserving items, especially perishable goods, at low temperatures by removing heat from a space or substance to lower and maintain its temperature below the ambient level. Air-conditioning systems typically include components like compressors, condensers, evaporator coils and refrigerant fluid. The system works by circulating refrigerant through a cycle of compression and expansion to absorb heat from indoor air and release it outside. The system also includes filters and fans to circulate and condition indoor air. Introduction Director - Medical Laboratory Medical Laboratory Technology (MLT) is a field of healthcare that involves the analysis of bodily fluids (like blood, urine, and cerebrospinal fluid), tissues, and cells to diagnose diseases, monitor treatments, and support medical research. The common tests performed include Complete Blood Count (CBC), Urinalysis, Blood Glucose Testing, Lipid Profile, Liver and Kidney Function Tests and Microbiological Cultures (e.g., for infections). They find employment in hospitals and clinics, diagnostic laboratories, public health facilities, research labs and blood banks. Over the past few years, the proliferation of laboratory automation has significantly decreased the hands-on nature of the work. Nowadays, many experienced laboratory technicians spend more time analyzing results, developing and modifying procedures, and establishing and monitoring quality control programs than they do performing tests. Director - Medical Laboratory: What’s the Career About? 157 Medical laboratory professionals are responsible for examining and analysing blood, body fluids, tissues, and cells in an effort to help clinicians determine the underlying cause of an

ssionals are responsible for examining and analysing blood, body fluids, tissues, and cells in an effort to help clinicians determine the underlying cause of an illness, the stage of a disease, or the effectiveness of therapy. To accomplish their objectives, laboratory scientists perform a wide variety of laboratory tests, often with the aid of complex, computerised, and automated instrumentation. Today, 70% of medical diagnoses is carried out in the laboratories by qualified medical laboratory professionals. There are several MLT specialties, and the duties for each of these roles may vary. For instance, MLTs who specialize in phlebotomy may have duties involving collecting, storing and analyzing blood samples. Other MLT specialties include: Microbiology professionals: Professionals in this role help microbiologists identify microorganisms, conduct experiments, maintain and prepare equipment, collect specimens for analysis, perform tests and prepare data reports. Hematology professionals: These technicians specialize in drawing, testing and analyzing blood to identify diseases of the blood and body tissues that form blood, and they keep laboratory equipment clean, calibrated and

rawing, testing and analyzing blood to identify diseases of the blood and body tissues that form blood, and they keep laboratory equipment clean, calibrated and sterile. Histotechnicians: These MLTs prepare thin samples of body tissues for a pathologist to examine with a microscope and check for signs of disease using dyes and other chemicals. Cytogenetic professionals: These specialists assist cytogenetic technologists in analyzing the structure of chromosomes in biological specimens and their relationship to diseases. Molecular biology lab professionals: MLTs in this field use specialized equipment to perform experiments on proteins and DNA under the supervision of molecular biologists and scientists. They also analyze data and record results. Cytology professionals: These technicians obtain cell samples and assist cytotechnologists in examining them for abnormalities that may lead to cancer or other diseases. Clinical chemistry professionals: These MLTs assist technologists in preparing specimens and analyzing the hormonal and chemical contents of body fluids, such as blood, urine or cerebrospinal fluid. Blood bank professionals (immunohematology technologists): MLTs with this

nal and chemical contents of body fluids, such as blood, urine or cerebrospinal fluid. Blood bank professionals (immunohematology technologists): MLTs with this specialty collect blood samples, label and classify them by type and prepare them and their components for transfusions or long-term storage. They also may determine compatibility of blood samples to screen potential donors.

Introduction Vice President (Sales) Selling is the process of persuading a potential customer to purchase a product, service, or idea in exchange for money or value. It involves a variety of activities, including finding potential customers, understanding their needs, presenting solutions, negotiating terms, and ultimately closing deals. In this entire scheme of things the most important role is that of sales people. They play a key role in identifying prospects, educating them about products or services, negotiating and closing deals. However, there are different types of sales approaches based on the business and nature of the customers. Some of them are: 176 1. Inside Sales: When sales teams engage with their prospects and customers remotely, often from their office, they follow an inside sales approach. This means they are selling from within their company. The company's inside sales persons contact leads and prospects to complete the traditional sales process — uncovering the customers' needs, matching them with the right solution, and closing the deal. 2. Outside Sales: On teams where salespeople visit and broker face-to-face deals with the prospect, they are following an

right solution, and closing the deal. 2. Outside Sales: On teams where salespeople visit and broker face-to-face deals with the prospect, they are following an outside sales approach. This implies that they are selling from outside their company. These teams tend to not have strictly regimented processes, allowing freedom and flexibility for the sales persons to develop and implement their own sales strategies. 3. B2B Sales: This common acronym stands for "business-to-business" and describes companies that sell products and services to other businesses, instead of individual consumers. B2B sales tend to have a higher sales value and more complex terms because the goods sold to other businesses typically play an essential role in how the buyer’s business operates. 4. B2C Sales: Unlike B2B sales, B2C (or business-to-consumer) sales revolve around transactions between a company and its individual consumers. These deals tend to be of lower price-value and complexity than B2B sales and can involve multiple deals with a variety of customers.

177 5. Business Development Sales Though business development doesn’t account for an entire sales transaction, it’s an important aspect of the sales function for many companies. This role is typically held by business development managers, who are responsible for generating new business and qualifying leads for their company. Once the business development managers have qualified the new leads, their sales persons can take the leads through the sales process to close the deal. 6. Agency Sales This type of sales involves generating and converting new leads to sign onto service packages from an agency. In the agency sales space, clients are typically signed either by project or on a retainer. For agencies that sign clients by project, they primarily focus on bringing in new business, selling service packages to new clients as their current projects wrap up. With a retainer model, agencies can engage with clients on an ongoing basis which allows for predictable recurring income with less dependence on bringing in a steady stream of new customers. 7. am of new customers. 7. With consultative selling, sales reps focus on building a relationship with the buyer and leading the sale with how the offering will benefit the individual customer, instead of solely focusing on the features of the product to make the sale. 8. Nutrition is the study of nutrients in food, how the body uses them, and the relationship between diet, health, and disease. Nutrients provide nourishment. Proteins, carbohydrates, fat, vitamins, minerals, fibre, and water are all nutrients. If people do not have the right balance of nutrients in their diet, their risk of developing certain health conditions increases. Nutrition is therefore a science that utilises concepts from molecular biology, biochemistry, and genetics to understand how nutrients affect the human body, guiding people toward healthy eating. Practitioners of nutrition are known as nutritionists, who advise people on how to lead healthier lifestyles and achieve health-related goals. Obesity has become a major problem across the world, and even children are no exception. Even for people at a healthy weight, a poor diet is associated with major health risks that can cause illness and even death. These include

en are no exception. Even for people at a healthy weight, a poor diet is associated with major health risks that can cause illness and even death. These include heart disease, hypertension (high blood pressure), type-2 diabetes, certain types of cancer and osteoporosis. Therefore, nutrition and dietetics have become extremely important field of healthcare. Chief Clinical Dietitian: What’s the Career About? 189 Dietetics is a field of science that determines how nutrition and good eating affect our overall health. It prepares students and practitioners to apply advanced knowledge of food and nutrition to help prevent and treat diseases, and maintain and promote health. It is people-oriented and science-focused; evidence-based and the first step toward a professional qualification. It involves creating individual nutritional therapies and meal plans to address specific health issues and designing nutrition programs for health care, educational, correctional and other institutions. Dietitians don’t just follow the newest diet trends and make standardised recommendations to their patients. Instead, they develop diet and nutrition programs tailored to an individual’s objectives and

iet trends and make standardised recommendations to their patients. Instead, they develop diet and nutrition programs tailored to an individual’s objectives and personal needs. Dieticians are qualified and regulated health professionals who assess, diagnose and treat dietary and nutritional problems at an individual and wider public-health level. They utilise the most up-to-date public health and scientific research on food, health, and disease, which they translate into practical guidance to enable people to make informed lifestyle and food choices. They can help one lose weight, manage food allergies, treat diet-related chronic diseases, and aid with malnutrition or insufficient intake. They also advise and influence food and health policy across the spectrum from government to local communities and individuals. Typically, dieticians deal more with clinical and therapeutic aspects of food intake. They are experts in identifying and treating disease-related malnutrition and in conducting medical nutrition therapy, for example, designing a tube feeding regimen. They often work as integral members of multi-disciplinary teams to treat complex clinical conditions such as diabetes,

xample, designing a tube feeding regimen. They often work as integral members of multi-disciplinary teams to treat complex clinical conditions such as diabetes, food allergy and intolerance, irritable bowel syndrome, eating disorders, chronic fatigue, kidney failure, malnutrition, and bowel disorders. Many dieticians work in hospitals and usually see specific patients where a nutritional assessment and intervention have been requested by a doctor or nurse, for example, if a patient has lost their ability to swallow or requires artificial nutrition due to intestinal failure.

It is the primary means of communication used to reach the vast majority of the general public. The media industry in turn can be defined as a varied collection of organisations that share the production, publication and distribution of information. The way that this information is shared varies massively, with some examples of media including radio, television, books, newspapers, magazines, social media, video games, film and music. 197 Traditional media is any form of mass communication that occurred before the introduction of the internet, e.g radio, newspapers, television and billboards. on Section, Reference Section, Periodicals Section, Maintenance Section, and the Administration & Finance Section. The newly acquired books are prepared for library use. For this purpose, these are classified, catalogued, entries filed in library catalogue and books shelved on display racks or in the stacks by the Technical Processing Section. Creative Director - Fashion Studies Fashion design is the art and practice of creating clothing, accessories, and footwear that are both functional and aesthetically pleasing. It involves a blend of creativity, technical skill, and cultural awareness to design garments that reflect personal or societal styles, trends, and identities. It involves translating creative ideas into tangible designs through various processes like sketching, pattern making, and garment construction. 209 Fashion design begins with an idea or inspiration—this could be drawn from art, history, nature, current events, or street fashion. Designs are then typically visualized through sketches, mood boards, and digital illustrations that show garment details, colours, and fabric choices. Designers choose appropriate fabrics, textures, and materials that align with their creative vision and the function of the garment. Choosing the right fabric and constructing the garment involves understanding various materials and techniques. To finish the designs the designers then get into the technical aspects that involve turning sketches into patterns, cutting fabrics, and constructing garments through sewing, draping,

e designers then get into the technical aspects that involve turning sketches into patterns, cutting fabrics, and constructing garments through sewing, draping, and fitting. Finished designs are often showcased in fashion shows, lookbooks, or online platforms. Marketing and branding help connect the designs with a target audience. The final stage involves overseeing the production of garments, sometimes involving collaborations with manufacturers or production houses. Introduction Fashion designers play a major role in our world. Their talent and vision play a big role in how people present themselves. Because of the time required to bring a garment onto the market, designers must at times anticipate changes to consumer desires. They thus influence society and the way they choose to express themselves. And so, they work in a variety of different ways in designing their pieces and accessories such as rings, bracelets and necklaces. Their talent and vision play a big role in how people look, and also contribute to the cultural and social environment. In all this, they are led by the Creative Directors. The entry level position in the field is that of an Assistant Fashion Designer. It is valuable in terms of gaining solid experience in the industry. This position is a way to get your foot in the door at a design studio, retail chain, or apparel manufacturing company, while earning a good salary, and it is a great way to establish a reputation in the industry. Assistant Fashion Designers are responsible for all aspects of the design and creation of new fashion products, as well as updating previous designs. They typically work under the supervision of a fashion designer and specialise in a particular area of design, such as skirts, sweaters, or (more generally) women’s apparel. They study fashion trends, sketch designs, select materials, and have a part in all the production aspects of the designs of the designers they work for.

210 After about 2-3 years of experience Assistant Fashion Designers become Fashion Designers who independently handles collections or segments under supervision, creates tech packs, liaises with merchandisers and suppliers, and participates in fittings and revisions. After 3 – 5 years of more experience Assistant Fashion Designers become Senior Fashion Designer/ Lead Designer who leads the creative process, mentors juniors, manages design calendars, and coordinates across teams for product development and execution. After another 3 – 7 years Assistant Fashion Designers become Design Manager/Creative Manager who oversees design teams, ensures design consistency across categories, aligns products with brand strategy, and approves final samples for production. Finally the Assistant Fashion Designer becomes a Creative Director/Head of Design who defines the creative direction for the brand or company. Creative Directors/Heads of Design make key decisions on design language, campaigns, collections, and public image. They also assist fashion designers and chief fashion designers with everything from designing clothes to preparing for fashion shows. Depending on the size of the company

Assistant Fashion Designers may coordinate meetings, assist at meetings with clients or retailers, attend fashion shows and trade shows, and assist with managing other workers as needed. It combines physical postures (asanas), breathing techniques (pranayama), and meditation (dhyana) to promote physical, mental, and spiritual well-being. The word yoga means "union" in Sanskrit, symbolizing the integration of mind, body, and spirit. It comes from the Sanskrit root "yuj," meaning "to join" or "to yoke," reflecting the practice's aim to unify the individual self with universal consciousness. Encourage self-realization: A master is considered to have achieved a high level of self-mastery and helps students work toward their own self-realization. Tailor guidance to individuals: Rather than offering a one-size-fits-all class, a master can provide personalized guidance, or even initiatory mantras, to help students with their individual spiritual development. Daycare Manager - Early Childhood Care & Education Early childhood education describes the period of learning that takes place from birth to 8 years old. It is a time of remarkable growth with brain development at its peak. During this stage, children are highly influenced by the environment and the people that surround them. It is therefore an important time for the children because it is during this time that children first learn how to interact with others, including peers, teachers and parents, and also begin to develop interests that will stay with them throughout their lives. It’s a time when children learn critical social and emotional skills too. 222 Early childhood education is more than preparation for primary school. It aims at the holistic development of a child’s social, emotional, cognitive and physical needs in order to build a solid and broad foundation for lifelong learning and wellbeing. Early childhood programs include any type of educational program that serves children in the preschool years and is designed to improve later school performance. They are also known by a variety of names, including nursery, preschool and pre-kindergarten. Early childhood

Early childhood education can produce significant gains in children's learning and development. High quality early childhood education assists many at-risk children in avoiding poor outcomes, such as dropping out of school. Although the benefits seem to cross all economic and social lines, the most significant gains are almost always noted among children from families with the lowest income levels and the least amount of formal education. Other long-term benefits include decrease in crime by children and increased attendance in schools leading to secondary and senior secondary school graduation. Introduction Data Science – Data Architect Several exabytes (1 exabyte = 10,000,000,000,000,000,000 bytes) of data is generated across the world every year. Add to that data that has been generated in the previous years ever since humanity started keeping track of the data in its experience. How does this data get stored, managed, processed, analysed and transformed into information? That is precisely what Data Science does. Data science is an inter-disciplinary field that uses scientific methods, processes, algorithms and systems to extract knowledge and insights from different structured and unstructured data. It involves developing methods of recording, storing, extracting, processing and analyzing data to obtain desired information. The goal of data science is to uncover patterns and trends in data for informed decision-making and gain insights and knowledge from any type of data —structured and unstructured. It employs techniques and theories drawn from many fields such as Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence and Management to analyze data and make predictions. As a result it has several applications in e-commerce, retail, healthcare, finance,

Artificial Intelligence and Management to analyze data and make predictions. As a result it has several applications in e-commerce, retail, healthcare, finance, marketing, and technology. Most common techniques used in data science are data mining, data analysis, data modeling, machine learning, algorithms, and visualization and most people who work in this field need to be having strong skills in programming, statistics, math, and business analytics. The first step in making a career in the field of data science is to join the team as a Data Analyst. Design Thinking and Innovation Design thinking is a human-centred, iterative problem- solving approach used to create innovative solutions by understanding user needs and iteratively developing and testing ideas. It's a way to make goods, services, and processes that meet real user needs by combining empathy, creativity, and problem-solving. It refers to the set of mental, strategic, and practical steps that designers use to make things, as well as the body of knowledge that has been created on how people think about design problems. It's used to learn about users, try hypotheses, reframe problems, and come up with new ways to solve them. It is most useful to tackle ill-defined or unknown problems and involves five phases: Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype and Test. 258 Prescriptions for the innovation of goods and services in commercial and social contexts are also linked to design thinking. In fact, design thinking actually encourages innovation. In a world that is changing quickly, businesses need to innovate to stay alive and competitive. Cross-functional teams collaborate to comprehend user demands and develop solutions that meet those needs as part of design thinking.

Additionally, the design thinking method facilitates the discovery of creative solutions. In fact, big businesses like Google, Apple, and Airbnb leverage design thinking's useful techniques and resources to spur innovation. Businesses in a variety of sectors, including technology, services, engineering, and architecture, have all adopted the approach to spur innovation and tackle challenging issues. The design thinking process aims to satisfy three criteria: Criteria 2: Feasibility - Be Technologically Possible Once the team comes up with one or more solutions, they evaluate whether it is implementable. In theory, any solution is feasible if the organization has infinite resources and time to build it. However, given the team’s present (or future resources), the team assesses if the solution is worth going ahead with. At this juncture, the team may

At this juncture, the team may iterate on the solution to make it more feasible or increase its resources (say, hire more personnel or bring in specialized tools). It is recommended that at the start of the design thinking process, teams should not get too stuck up in the technical implementation. This is because if teams start with technical constraints, they might restrict innovation. Criteria 1: Desirability - Meet People’s Needs The design thinking process starts by examining the needs, dreams and behaviours of people—the end users and understanding them. The design team listens with empathy what people want, not what the organisation thinks they want or need for this. The team then ideates solutions to satisfy these needs from the end user’s point of view. Teams usually start with desirability and then bring in the other two criteria.

259 The Five Stages of Design Thinking: One of the commonly used design processes has five phases: Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype, and Test. These stages are not always sequential. Their aim is to help the team gain a deep understanding of the users and their ideal solution/product. Teams often run them in parallel, out of order, and repeat them as needed. Criteria 3: Viability - Generate Profits A desirable and technically feasible product isn’t enough. The organisation must be able to generate revenues and profits from the solution. Viability is essential not only for commercial organizations but also for non-profits. Traditionally, organisations begin with feasibility or viability and then try to find a problem to fit the solution and push it to the market. Design thinking reverses this process and advocates that teams begin with desirability and bring in the other two criteria later. Stage 1: Empathize—Research Users' Needs: Empathy is crucial to design thinking because it allows designers to set aside assumptions they may have and gain insight into users and their needs. So the team works toward understanding the problem, typically through user research. Stage 2:

Stage 2: Define—State Users' Needs and Problems: Once the team collects the information they need, they analyse the observations and define the core problems. These definitions are called problem statements. At this point the team may also create personas to help keep efforts human-centered. Stage 3: Ideate—Challenge Assumptions and Create Ideas: With the foundation in place, teams gear up to “think outside the box.” They brainstorm multiple ways to view the problem and identify innovative solutions to it. Stage 4: Prototype—Start to Create Solutions: This is an experimental phase. The goal of this phase is to identify the best possible solution for each problem. The team produces inexpensive, scaled-down versions of the product (or specific features found within the product) to investigate the ideas e.g. paper prototypes. Stage 5: Test—Try the Solutions Out: The team tests these prototypes with real users to evaluate if they solve the problem. However, by paying close attention, one can spot issues based on actual user behavior rather than just refining their conceptions of the user. This facilitates the definition of unclear issues, which in turn facilitates the development of solutions. Leads to more innovative solutions: o People cannot ask for things that do not yet exist because they are incapable of conceptualizing things that are not thought to be possible. In essence, design thinking helps turn problems into opportunities by keeping people at the centre of the solution process. Let us now understand innovation. Innovation is the process of creating or implementing something new or improved. In essence, innovation is about making things better or more effective, whether it's a new technology, a refined process, or a fresh approach to a problem. It goes beyond just having a good idea—innovation means turning ideas into real-world impact. Introduction A Career in Logistics Logistics is the management of the flow and storage of goods, services, and information from the point of origin to the point of consumption to meet customer requirements. All raw materials, in-process and finished inventory, and order information are included in the flow, both forward and backwards, and storage between the place of origin and client delivery. Efficient logistics ensures products are moved, stored, and delivered in the right condition, at the right time, and at the right cost. Warehousing: The strategic storage of goods involves activities like receiving, organising, and managing inventory in warehouses and distribution centres to ensure quick access for order fulfilment. Transportation management: This involves selecting the most efficient modes of transport —such as road, rail, sea, or air—and optimising routes to reduce costs, transit times, and fuel consumption. The key components of logistics are: Order fulfilment: Encompassing the entire process from a customer placing an order to its delivery, this includes picking, packing, and shipping the products. Inventory management: This is the process of tracking stock levels to

acing an order to its delivery, this includes picking, packing, and shipping the products. Inventory management: This is the process of tracking stock levels to prevent overstocking (which ties up capital) and understocking (which can lead to lost sales). It uses data and demand forecasting to maintain optimal inventory leve. 264 Packaging: A vital part of logistics, proper packaging ensures that products are protected during transport and storage and that it uses space efficiently.

265 Importance of logistics Risk management: Identifying and mitigating risks associated with the movement and storage of goods. Information flow and technology: Modern logistics relies on the seamless flow of data to enable real-time tracking, optimise processes, and enhance decision-making through software and automation. Types of Logistics Depending on the nature of the movement of materials, there are four types of logistics: 1.Inbound Logistics – Managing the movement of materials and supplies coming into a business (e.g., raw materials from suppliers). 2.Outbound Logistics – Managing the movement of finished goods out of a business (e.g., delivering products to customers). 3.Reverse Logistics – Handling returns, recycling, and disposal of products. 4.Third-Party Logistics (3PL) – Outsourcing logistics functions to specialised companies. Logistics is important for the following reasons:: Cost efficiency: Efficient logistics reduces costs through optimized transportation, warehousing, and inventory management. Customer satisfaction: It ensures that customers receive their orders on time and in good condition, which is crucial for customer satisfaction and loyalty.

Competitiveness: Effective logistics helps businesses stay competitive by enabling them to reach wider markets and respond quickly to customer needs. Enabling trade: Logistics is the backbone of both domestic and international trade, allowing for the movement of raw materials and finished products across the globe. Career Options in Logistics Logistics is one of the fastest-growing career fields globally, driven by e-commerce, manufacturing, and international trade. It offers roles ranging from operations and analytics to management and technology. Here are some of the career options in logistics:

1.Transportation and Distribution 266 These professionals make sure goods move efficiently from one place to another. Transportation Manager – Plans routes, selects carriers, and optimizes delivery costs. Fleet Manager – Manages a company’s vehicles and drivers. Dispatcher – Coordinates truck schedules and shipment tracking. Route Planner / Logistics Coordinator – Designs efficient delivery routes and monitors shipments. 2. Warehousing and Inventory Management Focused on storage, handling, and inventory control. Warehouse Manager – Oversees operations, safety, and workforce in warehouses. Inventory Analyst / Controller – Tracks stock levels and prevents shortages or overstocking. Material Handler / Storekeeper – Physically manages goods in storage facilities. Distribution Center Supervisor – Manages order picking, packing, and shipping. 3. Supply Chain and Procurement These roles ensure smooth coordination between suppliers, manufacturers, and customers. Supply Chain Manager – Oversees end-to-end movement of materials and products. Procurement / Purchasing Manager – Buys raw materials or products at the best quality and price. Logistics Analyst / Data Analyst – Uses data to optimize costs and improve performance. Systems Support Specialist – Manages logistics software (like SAP, Oracle, or WMS). Automation & Robotics Engineer – Designs warehouse automation systems. Freight Forwarder – Arranges global shipment of goods across borders. Customs Broker – Ensures imports/exports comply with regulations. Import/Export Manager – Manages documentation, tariffs, and trade compliance. Global Logistics Manager – Coordinates supply chains across countries. 6. Operations Research Analyst – Uses math and simulations for process optimisation. Trainer / Academic / Researcher – Teaches or studies logistics systems.

267 The future of the logistics industry is characterized by significant growth and a fundamental transformation driven by technology, sustainability, and evolving consumer demands. As goods are moved, stored, and delivered in an increasingly interconnected world, logistics is evolving from a back-end process into a core strategic function for businesses. Future Prospects The logistics industry offers stable and dynamic career paths, with many new roles emerging due to technological advancements. Some of these are: Logistics Technology Specialist: Experts who can implement, integrate, and optimize technology like warehouse management systems (WMS), transport management systems (TMS), blockchain, and IoT. Supply Chain Analyst: Professionals who use data and analytics to optimize supply chain operations, improve forecasting, and enhance risk management. Warehouse Operations Manager: With increasing automation, these managers oversee and integrate human and robotic workflows for maximum efficiency.
